sources_considered.why: Direct evaluation of models checking their own generated news claims, including a setting without retrieval.
Read Tables 3 and 5 to distinguish self-evaluation, false-claim detection, errors, and abstentions.
Relevant controlled work on detecting and correcting generated factual errors, but it adds trained probing heads.
Postdates the observation period and concerns mathematical answer verification.

evidence_items.publisher: Jiayi Yao, Haibo Sun and Nianwen Xue / arXiv
evidence_items.explanation: In the no-retrieval self-evaluation setting, Table 5 reports correct assessments for 201 of 532 false GPT-generated claims and 229 of 537 false GLM-generated claims. Substantial abstention remains, but identifying these errors contradicts the claimed absence of meaningful self-fact-checking ability.

DSVD reports improved factuality using internal-state probes and rollback. Because the detector receives additional training using known answers, this is context about available internal signals rather than decisive evidence of an unaided model’s self-checking ability.

unresolved_gaps: The studies do not operationalize or isolate superficial understanding as the causal explanation.
Exact experiment dates are not disclosed; event dates use the report year.
The direct study covers a limited set of models and generated news claims.
